subject: Proposal: phased commit, conversion-credit cadence & temporary capacity safeguard
messages:
From: Anna Patel <anna@skylinehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity — sizing, conversion credits, and short-term capacity ask

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Skyline is evaluating a move from hosted API to a Dedicated pool for our clinical inference workloads and we want to understand how Redwood would structure conversion credits, phased commits, and any temporary capacity protections while we ramp. A few things we want priced/confirmed: 

- Typical commit phasing for a 12‑month reserved contract (we expect to start smaller and ramp).
- Conversion credit mechanics: how you translate existing hosted spend into Dedicated credits and how long credits last.
- Short-term capacity safeguard / bridge months while we onboard integrations (we expect uneven peaks during months 0–3).
- GPU sizing guidance: we expect up to ~30M tokens/day at peak across latency targets for clinical prompts; want a recommended pool and expected throughput SLOs.

Attached is the RFP summary and our early usage profile (Skyline_RFP_2026.pdf). Can you put together a pragmatic pricing sketch we can send to procurement? Procurement will need clear language about guaranteed throughput, overage rates, and an SLA for initial onboarding months.

Appreciate it — looking to share a proposal with procurement by next week.

Thanks,
Anna
Anna Patel
Director, ML Platform
Skyline Health
anna@skylinehealth.com

Attachment: Skyline_RFP_2026.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Patel <anna@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 12:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing, conversion credits, and short-term capacity ask

Hi Anna — great to connect. Pasting a concise proposal below so procurement has something concrete to react to; attaching a one‑page sketch as well (20260528-jordan-pricing-outline.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if useful.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Commit term: 12 months (option to true-up monthly). Tiered commit bands (entry / mid / enterprise) with step-down unit price as commit increases.
- Conversion credits: we propose converting hosted spend to an upfront credit applied to the first 3 billing months of Dedicated. Example: hosted spend of $120k/month -> $360k conversion credit applied across months 0–3 at 66/33/0% taper (month0: 66%, month1: 33%, month2: 0%). We can adjust cadence depending on the size of the conversion.
- Temporary capacity safeguard ("onramp burst pool"): for months 0–3 we reserve a burst buffer of additional GPU capacity at a reduced one-time activation fee plus usage-based billing for consumption above committed baseline. This protects you from being throttled during integration spikes without requiring a larger committed pool from day 1.
- GPU pool sizing: based on the profile in your RFP (peak ~30M tokens/day), our recommendation is an initial pool equivalent to 8 high‑throughput accelerators (A100-class equivalent) with an onramp burst pool sized to cover 40–60% additional peak for months 0–3. We will run an intake evaluation to refine the exact vGPU mix.
- Throughput & SLOs: guaranteed baseline throughput (median and 95th percentile thresholds) for pinned model versions. We typically offer: 99th percentile latency SLO tied to token length bands and a throughput floor (tokens/sec) per pool; overage pricing triggers if sustained usage above a 2x baseline occurs for a rolling 7‑day window.
- Pricing sketch: committed unit price + reserved pool fee + small activation fee for the burst pool. Overage rates are defined per token above committed throughput.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Procurement-ready one-pager (attached) + a short legal addendum draft (we'll produce).
2) Intake call with your engineering team this week to validate token distributions and sample payloads so we can size GPUs more precisely.
3) If you need a longer bridge, we can extend the conversion credit taper and increase burst pool months to 4 at a small incremental fee.

If this direction looks OK, Marissa — can you please prepare redline suggestions for the credit cadence and the exact SLA language we should include? Rishi — can you validate the suggested GPU mix / burst sizing?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 14:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — sizing, conversion credits, and short-term capacity ask

Jordan / Rishi — quick internal notes before we send to procurement: 

- Credit cadence: recommend stronger upfront conversion credit in month0 for faster time-to-value (example alternative: 75% / 25% / 0% instead of 66/33/0 for small-to-mid deals).
- Burst pool: define max burst (absolute tokens/sec) and a clear activation trigger so procurement can audit when they will pay usage-based rates; include a weekly usage dashboard requirement during months 0–3.
- SLA language: add a "soft pause" clause — if sustained overload occurs, we move traffic to a queued/backoff mode for 30 minutes and notify, then open burst if activated. Also add an explicit true-up cadence (monthly) and a 30‑day notice to scale committed pool up/down.
- GPU mix: I agree with 8x A100-equivalent start; add an option for 16x A10 as a cost-sensitive variant.

I'll attach redlines (redlines_pricing.xlsx) with suggested percentages and the legal wording to include. Jordan — once Anna confirms acceptance of the cadence option, we should get procurement on a call to lock the DocuSign timeline.

-Marissa
VP, Solutions & Pricing
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: phased commit, conversion-credit cadence & temporary capacity safeguard

Jordan / Marissa — thanks for the thoughtful sketch and rapid turnaround. Procurement looped me in; a couple of items before we route to legal: 

- We prefer the alternative credit cadence you offered in the note (75%/25%/0) if you can make it work for our hosted conversion size.
- Please extend the burst pool window to 4 months (months 0–3 inclusive of onboarding and month 4 as a safety taper) if we commit to at least two integration partners and share integration runbooks.
- We need a weekly usage dashboard (read-only link) for the first 12 weeks.
- Please add a simple overage cap for months 0–4 (max overage charge not to exceed 50% of the committed monthly fee) — procurement requests this to limit surprise costs while we tune prompts.

If you can incorporate those items, procurement has asked that we receive a DocuSign-ready agreement and a final one-pager by next Tuesday. I'm forwarding procurement to you on this thread.

Procurement contact: procurement@skylinehealth.com

Thanks — Anna
Anna Patel
